items.title_orig: 10 candid photos from Pearl Jam's early years taken by bassist Jeff Ament
items.article_text:
From dusty basements to the White House: Pearl Jam’s Jeff Ament digs through decades of lost negatives, candid tour photos and memories

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

For the past 25 years, Pearl Jam bassist Jeff Ament had been looking at the boxes in his basement that were full of decomposing contact sheets and negatives, shot on film from the formative years of Pearl Jam, and wondering what he should do with them.

“A big reason I took all those photos was because we had a newsletter that we sent out to fans that always needed content,” Ament remembers. “Photographers were expensive, so I just did it myself. I wasn’t even thinking about the fact that I was documenting anything.”

Jeff and his brother, Barry, who’s been working with Pearl Jam as a designer since the early 90s, went through the images to digitise them, and it was Barry who suggested that they should be made into a book.

“I used to joke that if I ever write a book, shoot me!” laughs Ament. “Eighty per cent of rock’n’roll books are not great. Most are written by ghostwriters, so you don’t really hear the voice of the artist, and sometimes they’re too gossipy and don’t have enough magic. So I didn’t want this to be a full-on memoir.”

Instead, Since Forever is composed primarily of photos, with snippets of text from Ament’s journals, memories and dreams.

“The book ended up being a thank-you letter to everybody,” he says. “I’m so grateful to my bandmates, the crew and everyone I went on this ride with.”

"This was our first bus; it would have been in October or November 1991. We found out on short notice that we’d gotten a tour with the Red Hot Chili Peppers, so we had to cut our own tour short. I remember someone saying, ‘Hey man, the bus is here,’ and we all ran out like little kids – like if your parents bought a Winnebago or a camper van. It was pretty joyous.”

"That was the first trip that the band took to New York, before our album [Ten] came out. I think we played Wetlands, which was this small place. I remember only Stone and I had been in New York before, just briefly with Mother Love Bone and Green River, so we were all so excited to be in New York. This picture looks like it could be Broadway; there’s a good chance we were walking to Tower Records.

"You can tell it’s early days because Mike is wearing a Pearl Jam shirt! I have no idea who the two people in the background are. Those early pictures, man. I feel like you can see how excited we were to be in a city where so many of our heroes made art and music.”
